messages:
sara: Quick triage thread: onboarding v4-ranker showed mixed signals across datasets after we switched candidate formatting + rolled int8 PTQ. ndcg up on some benches, MRR down on others. need checklist and reproducible diffs.
dmitri: can you share the benches and exact quant settings?
sara: summary first (holdout P/Q/R are three different user cohorts):
```
model: v4-ranker (ptq int8 symmetric per-tensor)
format old: newline delimiter between candidates
format new: JSON array stringified
Holdout P: ndcg@10 0.295 -> 0.303 (+2.7%), mrr@10 0.185 -> 0.180 (-2.8%)
Holdout Q: ndcg@10 0.342 -> 0.335 (-2.0%), mrr@10 0.212 -> 0.204 (-3.8%)
Holdout R: ndcg@10 0.278 -> 0.286 (+2.9%), mrr@10 0.162 -> 0.160 (-1.2%)
```
sara: pattern: nDCG sometimes up, MRR consistently down or flat.
kevin: interesting that Q regresses both metrics. could be dataset-specific tokenization artifacts or candidate length distributions.
dmitri: ACTION: run controlled tokenization parity test (pre-tokenize prompt+candidate strings and feed token IDs). if metrics converge, formatting->tokenization is root cause.
sara: already on it. pre-tokenization test will run tonight.
kevin: also run quant-variant sweep: fp32, int8 symmetric, int8 per-channel, and int4 hybrid if harness supports. PTQ vs QAT?
dmitri: include both static calibration sets: (a) dev sampled uniformly, (b) dev biased to long queries. calibration can change clipping/scales.
sara: good point. small note: our PTQ pipeline uses per-tensor symmetric by default; we have per-channel option but slower. will enable per-channel for one run.
eval-bot: small run results (1000 queries sample) uploaded: s3://redwood-eval/tmp/v4-format-quant-sample.csv
sara: thanks @eval-bot. i glanced: fp32 baseline shows minimal MRR drop (<0.5%) between formats. int8 symmetric shows largest MRR drop (~3-4%). int8 per-channel reduces delta to ~1.2%. int4 catastrophic on some tails.
kevin: that suggests quantization amplification of token-boundary effects. hypothesis: JSON quoting/escaping increases prefix length, shifting where important tokens fall relative to positional attention and KV cache. quantization nonlinearity then amplifies small logit shifts.
dmitri: to validate: 1) measure per-query token-count delta between formats and correlate with MRR delta 2) compute per-query top-1 logit difference fp32->int8 per format 3) run a quick ablation replacing quotes with an explicit safe delimiter token like <C> to see if tokenization boundaries fix it
sara: I'll produce correlation plot. early look: queries where prefix tokens increase >8 tend to have worst MRR drops.
eval-bot: attached small CSV columns: query_id, prefix_tokens_old, prefix_tokens_new, top1_fp32_logit, top1_int8_logit, top1_change, top1_label_match_old, top1_label_match_new
kevin: thumbs-up. another idea: rerank scoring sometimes uses pairwise comparison formatting (QA prompt that enumerates candidates). Did we switch to a single concatenated string? if so, the model's relative attention across candidates might shift.
sara: yes we concatenated. old approach enumerated with numeric bullets, new JSON array collapsed structure. no per-candidate separators besides JSON punctuation.
dmitri: low-effort mitigation: insert explicit separator token between candidates before stringifying JSON, e.g., <DOC_START> and <DOC_END>, or add a short ASCII marker that tokenizes to single token for our tokenizer.
sara: i'll test adding '<DOC>' wrapper inside the JSON strings.
eval-bot: quick test (500 queries): adding <DOC> recovered ~70% of MRR delta on int8 symmetric; ndcg maintained the modest gains.
kevin: great. that suggests formatting itself is the main lever and quantization amplifies.
dmitri: long-term: update onboarding checklist and docs: when changing candidate formatting, run quant-sweep and tokenization parity tests, and prefer per-channel quantization for production when format changes are likely.
sara: I'll draft the checklist PR. also propose a small addition to optimize: a formatting-safety rule that encourages explicit delimiter tokens when customers provide JSON arrays as input to avoid invisible boundary artifacts under quantization.
kevin: consider adding a unit test in the rerank CI: for any formatting change, run a tiny holdout to assert top-1 match rate doesn't drop more than X% between formats for fp32/int8.
sara: agreed. adding to PR.
ops-bot: canary pause for v4-ranker new-format until triage complete.
sara: final note: we should check if any downstream analytics/metrics are more top-1 sensitive (CTR/perf). ops wants a rollback threshold if top-1 drop >2% on production traffic.
dmitri: will draft rollback threshold proposal and link here.
sara: attaching triage artifacts (s3 links) and will update when full pre-tokenized run finishes. :email:
